newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Hub Power in full production.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Hub Power in full production.

text.p: The Hub Power Company Ltd (HUBCO) announced on Friday it had started full commercial production from its 1,292-megawatt-power plant, 25 days ahead of schedule, adding it had saved $300 million in construction.

"We have started full commercial production," Philip Spencer, director of operations, told Reuters. "The company has achieved savings of $300 million as it spent $1.5 billion out of available funds of $1.8 billion," he added.
The fourth and last generator, with a capacity of 323 megawatts (MW), came on stream on Thursday at Hub near Karachi.
Spencer said HUBCO would now supply 1,200 MW to the national grid, adding 13 percent to Pakistan's installed capacity of 12,600 MW. The company will save 92 MW for its own use.
A HUBCO statement said three generators had been completed in the past eight months and were already in commercial production.
The plant, operated and maintained by National Power Plc of Britain, was built under a turnkey contract by a consortium led by Mitsui Construction of Japan.
Other members of the consortium included Campenon Bernard of France, Ansaldo Energia of Italy, and Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries Co Ltd of Japan, the statement said.
Funding for the project was through a combination of debt and through equity, the statement said. "The senior debt is held by a consortium of 44 offshore and nine onshore banks."
The subordinated debt has been subscribed by the World Bank, the Export-Import Bank of Japan, and the governments of Japan, France, Italy and the United States, the statement said.
It said the power station was the first private sector infrastructure project in Pakistan and the first lending by the World Bank and Japan's Exim Bank to such a project.
The company has been incorporated in Pakistan and its shares are traded on the country's three stock exchanges and in Luxembourg as global depositary receipts (GDRs).
The company's two largest promoting shareholders are Xenel Industries Ltd of Saudi Arabia and National Power.
